analysis_sections.label: Discussion

significance_by_specialty.medonc: Durable ~7-yr rPFS gains with triplet held in both volume strata (interaction p = 0.5552), so volume alone does not gate abiraterone added to ADT + docetaxel in de novo mCSPC. studies.name: CCTG PR21 (QoL)
studies.tldr: FACT-P total change wk 30 -8.3 Doc vs +4.7 LuP (p<0.001) in post-ARPI mCRPC; earlier analysis found no significant rPFS difference.
details: 🔍 Randomized phase II, Doc vs 177Lu-PSMA-617 in mCRPC after prior ARPI
📊 Primary endpoint rPFS: no significant difference between arms (no effect size reported in source)
🔍 189 of 199 randomized pts started treatment (n=94 LuP; n=95 Doc)
🔍 QoL analysis required baseline plus ≥1 on-treatment FACT-P questionnaire
🔍 FACT-P every 6 wks on therapy, every 12 wks prior to cross-over; TOI pre-specified

details.text: 📊 Mean change from baseline, Doc vs LuP

rows: High GP5 side-effect bother, any time

details: 📐 Mixed model: treatment-by-visit interaction for TOI, FACT-P, FACT-G (each p<0.01); Doc worsened, LuP stable
📊 FACT-G and physical well-being trajectories also favored LuP (per UroToday)
📊 MCID analysis: worse scores for Doc at wk 24 vs wk 12 for FACT-P total and TOI
⚠️ Completion 96% at baseline but only >70% at most later time-points; arm separation emerges wk 24-36
⚠️ Blinding not stated; self-reported QoL with visibly different treatments invites expectation bias
⚠️ Null rPFS in a phase II is not equivalence; trial not described as non-inferiority
⚠️ GP5 comparison descriptive only; no test reported

verdict.rationale: Randomized phase II; QoL is a secondary analysis of a trial whose null rPFS was not designed to show equivalence. PRO gap arises late, when completion falls.
verdict.audience: mCRPC after prior ARPI, taxane-naive for mCRPC presumed by design

studies.significance: The QoL gap is not front-loaded: TOI and total FACT-P separate at wk 24-36, with FACT-P total -8.3 vs +4.7 at wk 30, and high side-effect bother in 40.7% vs 15.4%. For a reader delivering RLT, this is the first randomized PRO data placing LuP against docetaxel rather than an ARPI switch or cabazitaxel, though activity and cycle number are not reported in source.
studies.monday_clinic: In mCRPC progressing after an ARPI where docetaxel and LuP are both on the table, this supports weighing patient-reported tolerability toward LuP; it does not establish equal disease control, and does not extend to post-taxane disease.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: **Randomized phase II** (CCTG PR21), Doc vs 177Lu-PSMA-617; **primary endpoint rPFS showed no significant difference**. This report is the QoL comparison, with the **FACT-P TOI pre-specified**.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: **mCRPC after prior ARPI**. 189 of 199 randomized pts started treatment (n=94 LuP, n=95 Doc); QoL analysis required **baseline plus ≥1 on-treatment questionnaire**. Baseline scores similar between arms.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: FACT-P every 6 wks on therapy and every 12 wks before cross-over, analyzed over the **36-wk treatment period** by mean change from baseline and a linear mixed model with treatment-by-visit interaction. GP5 item (side-effect bother) described by proportion scoring 3 or 4.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: Mixed model showed **worsening over time with Doc and stability with LuP** for TOI, FACT-P and FACT-G (each p<0.01). FACT-G, physical well-being and the MCID analysis also favored LuP.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: LuP activity, cycle number and schedule are **not reported in source**, nor is the docetaxel schedule, so dose transferability cannot be judged from this abstract.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: VISION tested LuP added to standard care post-taxane, TheraP tested LuP against cabazitaxel post-docetaxel, and PSMAfore tested LuP against an ARPI change in taxane-naive disease. PR21 is the head-to-head against **docetaxel itself** in the post-ARPI setting, the comparison those trials left open.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents mCRPC pts after prior ARPI who were candidates for either docetaxel or LuP. Does not represent post-taxane mCRPC or castration-sensitive disease.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Questionnaire completion fell from **96%** at baseline to **>70%** at most later time-points, and the arm separation appears at wk 24-36, when dropout from progression or toxicity can be informative. Blinding is not stated, and the GP5 difference is descriptive with no test reported.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The data make tolerability a defensible tie-breaker when the two agents are both options. They do not settle whether LuP matches docetaxel on disease control, because a null rPFS in a phase II is not an equivalence result.

studies.interpretation:
The value of this analysis depends almost entirely on how one reads the parent trial. PR21 found no significant rPFS difference between docetaxel and Lu-PSMA-617 in men with mCRPC after an androgen receptor pathway inhibitor. If that null is read as rough parity on disease control, the QoL data become decisive: a treatment that controls disease about as well and costs patients less in symptom burden is the obvious choice. But a randomized phase II with a null primary endpoint is not a non-inferiority trial, and nothing in the source describes it as one. The honest reading is that PR21 did not detect an efficacy difference, which leaves room for a clinically relevant one in either direction. The QoL result strengthens the case for LuP as a reasonable option; it does not convert an underpowered null into equivalence.

The QoL signal itself is internally coherent. The pre-specified TOI, total FACT-P and FACT-G all move the same way, the mixed-model interaction is consistent across domains (each p<0.01), and the item-level side-effect bother result (40.7% vs 15.4%) points the same direction as the composite scales. The MCID analysis, per the UroToday report, also favors LuP. Concordance across instruments makes a chance finding less likely than if one domain at one visit had crossed p<0.05.

The pattern in time deserves scrutiny. The arms separate at weeks 24, 30 and 36, not early. That fits the expected cumulative toxicity of docetaxel, but it is also the window in which questionnaire completion has fallen from 96% toward the >70% floor and in which pts who progress or stop treatment drop out of the on-treatment assessments. If the pts remaining in the LuP arm at week 30 are a fitter subset, the stability of that arm partly reflects who is still answering. The abstract does not report how missingness differed by arm or whether sensitivity analyses addressed it. Blinding is not stated either; with an IV chemotherapy and a radioligand given on different schedules with different visible toxicities, expectation effects on self-reported side-effect bother are hard to exclude.

Against the existing randomized LuP literature, PR21 fills a specific gap. VISION established LuP on top of standard care after taxane exposure, TheraP compared it with cabazitaxel after docetaxel, and PSMAfore compared it with an ARPI switch in taxane-naive disease. None directly tested LuP against docetaxel, which is the realistic alternative for many post-ARPI pts. PR21 is therefore the first randomized PRO comparison at that decision point, which is why it matters even with its limits.

What would make this wrong is a larger trial showing docetaxel controls disease meaningfully better, at which point the QoL advantage becomes a trade-off rather than a free benefit. Until then, the result supports tolerability as a legitimate factor in choosing LuP over docetaxel after an ARPI, without settling which agent should come first in sequence.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: For a reader delivering RLT, this is the first randomized PRO comparison of LuP against docetaxel post-ARPI: FACT-P total -8.3 vs +4.7 at wk 30, high side-effect bother 40.7% vs 15.4%. LuP activity and cycle count are not reported in source, so schedule transferability is unknown.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: For the post-ARPI mCRPC sequencing choice, docetaxel carried a measurable QoL cost (TOI -7.1 vs +2.8 at wk 30) with no detected rPFS gain. That supports offering LuP ahead of docetaxel on tolerability grounds, while the phase II null leaves efficacy parity unproven.

open_questions: Is LuP non-inferior to docetaxel on rPFS in an adequately powered trial?
Optimal sequencing of LuP and docetaxel after ARPI progression
Does differential questionnaire dropout explain the late QoL separation?

studies.name: PEACE-1
studies.tldr: At 7.7y median f/u, abiraterone OS HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.65-0.87, p=0.0001), mOS 4.6 vs 6.1y in de novo mCSPC.

details.text: 📊 Abiraterone effect by population at long-term f/u

details: 🔍 Phase 3, 2x2 factorial, 1:1:1:1, N=1,173 de novo mCSPC (57% high-, 43% low-volume)
🔍 Prespecified long-term analysis, median f/u 7.7y (range 7.5-7.9)
📊 High-volume 7y OS: 22.4% doublet vs 40.9% triplet
📊 Low-volume rPFS, triplet vs doublet: HR 0.54 (95% CI 0.32-0.91), 3.2y absolute benefit
📐 Triplet OS benefit independent of volume, interaction p=0.56

details.text: 📊 G3-4 AEs of interest, ADT + docetaxel vs + abiraterone
subdetails: No long-term safety signals per presenter

details: ⚠️ Docetaxel permitted by amendment, so the docetaxel subgroup is not randomized for docetaxel
⚠️ Low-volume OS CI crosses 1 (0.51-1.05)
🔗 vs STAMPEDE: docetaxel and abiraterone doublets gave similar OS, the rationale for the triplet

verdict.rationale: Prespecified long-term analysis of an open-label randomized phase 3 that confirms the primary analysis. The docetaxel subgroup was not randomized for docetaxel, and the low-volume OS CI crosses 1.
verdict.audience: De novo mCSPC, high- or low-volume, on ADT ± docetaxel

studies.significance: The RT finding is indirect. Abiraterone and RT showed no treatment interaction, so the OS gain (HR 0.75) held with or without prostate RT. The source gives no long-term OS or local endpoints for the RT arm. The primary analysis found no OS gain from RT, including low-volume, so RT in a triplet patient still rests on that earlier read.
studies.monday_clinic: In de novo mCSPC already on ADT + docetaxel, this supports adding abiraterone at either metastatic volume, with OS 4.4 vs 6.2y. It does not inform metachronous mCSPC or whether docetaxel adds anything over an ARPI doublet.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Open-label, 2x2 factorial phase 3, randomized 1:1:1:1, accrual 2013-2018. **Prespecified long-term analysis**, median f/u **7.7y** (range 7.5-7.9).

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: **De novo mCSPC**, N=1,173; 57% high-volume, 43% low-volume.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: SOC was ADT, with docetaxel permitted after a protocol amendment; 710 pts received **ADT + docetaxel**. Factorial randomization added abiraterone/prednisone and/or prostate RT.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: Prostate RT was a factorial arm. Dose and fractionation are not reported in the source. The primary analysis found **no OS gain from RT**, including low-volume, and the long-term analysis found **no abiraterone × RT interaction**.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: The OS benefit from abiraterone held at 7.7y and was **independent of metastatic volume** (interaction p=0.56). High-volume 7y OS was **22.4% vs 40.9%**, doublet vs triplet.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: G3-4 neutropenia was 12% vs 10% and hypertension **14% vs 21%** (ADT + docetaxel vs + abiraterone). The presenter reported no long-term safety signals.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: In STAMPEDE, the docetaxel and abiraterone doublets gave similar OS, which is why combining them was tested here. ARASENS addresses the same triplet question with a different ARPI. Most sponsor trials report 5 years of follow-up or less, so PEACE-1 now carries the longest triplet survival data.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents de novo mCSPC on ADT with or without docetaxel, at either metastatic volume. Does not represent metachronous mCSPC after prior local therapy.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Docetaxel use was physician-chosen after the amendment, so the triplet vs doublet comparison sits inside a non-randomized docetaxel subgroup. The CI levels (99.9%, 95.1%) are nonstandard, and the source does not explain them. It also gives the earlier analysis's median f/u as both 4.4y and 3.5y.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The OS benefit survived **86% ARPI use beyond progression** in controls, so early use beats later use. It does not settle whether docetaxel adds over an ARPI doublet, or whether low-volume OS reaches significance.

studies.interpretation:
The central question an extended follow-up can answer is whether an intensification benefit is real or only a borrowing of time that later salvage erases. PEACE-1 now answers it directly for abiraterone. Most of the control arm (86%) went on to receive an ARPI at progression, yet the overall survival advantage did not dissolve: HR 0.75 at a median of 7.7 years, with median survival moving from 4.6 to 6.1 years. That is the cleanest available evidence in de novo mCSPC that the timing of androgen receptor pathway inhibition matters, not merely exposure to it. A trial in which controls rarely crossed over would have left this open. This one cannot be explained away by withheld salvage.

The triplet signal deserves a more careful read than the presenter's framing. Docetaxel was not a randomized factor. It entered the protocol by amendment once its survival benefit was established, and the 710 patients on ADT plus docetaxel are those whose physicians chose it. Within that group, abiraterone was randomized, so the HR 0.68 is internally valid as abiraterone added to docetaxel. It does not show that a triplet beats an ARPI doublet without chemotherapy, and nothing in this source tests that. STAMPEDE showed that the two doublets produce similar survival. Whether docetaxel still earns its toxicity once an ARPI is given upfront remains the live question that ARASENS, a darolutamide triplet trial, also leaves unaddressed by design.

The volume analysis cuts both ways. The interaction p of 0.56 argues against a volume-specific effect, and the low-volume point estimate (HR 0.74) sits close to the high-volume one (HR 0.67). But the low-volume interval runs from 0.51 to 1.05. A reader who has historically reserved docetaxel for high-volume disease should treat the low-volume triplet benefit as consistent and plausible rather than proven. The 7-year survival figures in high-volume disease, 22.4% versus 40.9%, are where the presenter's claim of nearly doubled long-term survivors comes from. Those figures are subgroup estimates from a non-randomized chemotherapy stratum and should carry that discount.

For radiation oncologists, the long-term report adds one thing: abiraterone and prostate RT do not interact. The systemic benefit does not depend on whether the primary was irradiated, and RT does not blunt it. The source restates that the primary analysis found no OS benefit from RT, including in low-volume disease, but it provides no matured RT-arm survival or local endpoints. Any revised view of primary RT in low-volume de novo disease treated with modern triplet therapy will have to wait for that separate report.

Two technical oddities should temper confidence modestly: the unexplained 99.9% and 95.1% interval levels, and the inconsistent median follow-up quoted for the earlier analysis (4.4 versus 3.5 years). Neither changes the direction of the result, and both are likely reporting artifacts of a trade-press summary rather than flaws in the trial.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: Abiraterone and prostate RT showed no interaction, so the systemic OS gain holds with or without primary RT. The source reports no long-term RT-arm OS or local-control data, so the primary analysis's finding of no RT OS benefit, including low-volume, still frames the decision.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: With 7.7y f/u and 86% ARPI salvage in controls, early abiraterone still carries an OS benefit (HR 0.75). Adding it to ADT + docetaxel gave OS 4.4 vs 6.2y at either volume, but the low-volume OS CI crosses 1 and docetaxel was not randomized.

papers.title: Patient reported quality of life (QoL) for docetaxel (Doc) vs lutetium177-617-PSMA (LuP) for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC): Results from the Canadian cancer trials group (CCTG) PR21 trial
papers.abstract:
ESMO Congress 2026 abstract 2221RO · Rapid oral: Genitourinary tumours, prostate, penile and testis · 2026-10-23 · presented by Daniel J. Khalaf (Toronto, Canada) · NCT04663997

Background: CCTG PR21 is a phase II randomized clinical trial of Doc vs LuP for patients (pts) with mCRPC who have received prior androgen receptor pathway inhibitor. There was no significant difference in the primary endpoint of radiographic progression-free survival (rFPS). In this analysis, we present the comparison of QOL outcomes between treatment arms.
Methods: Inclusion required completion of baseline and minimum of one questionnaire on treatment. FACT-P questionnaire schedule was every 6 weeks (wks) on therapy and every 12 wks prior to cross-over. The FACT-P Trials Outcome Index (TOI) was a pre-specified outcome. For all FACT-P domains, we calculated the mean change from baseline at each timepoint during the 36-wk treatment period. A linear mixed model, with visit (wks from randomization), treatment arm, and treatment-by-visit interaction as the fixed effects, was utilized to compare the change in QOL domains over time. Pts’ scores on the GP5 item (“I am bothered by side effects of treatment”) were described by the distribution of high scores (3 or 4) by arm.
Results: 189 of 199 randomized patients started treatment (n=94 LuP; n=95 Doc). Questionnaire completion rates were 96% at baseline and exceeded 70% for most time-points. Baseline scores were similar between arms. Mean change for TOI was worse for Doc vs LuP at wk 24 (-4.1 vs +0.5, p=0.041) and wk 30 (-7.1 vs +2.8, p<0.001) and for total FACT-P at wk 24 (-4.8 vs +1.2, p=0.024), wk 30 (-8.3 vs +4.7, p<0.001) and wk 36 (-8.9 vs +1.5, p=0.027). The mixed model showed a significant interaction between treatment arm and visit, with worsening over time for Doc and stability for LuP for most domains including TOI, FACT-P, and FACT-G (each p<0.01). The proportion of pts reporting high GP5 score at any time was 40.7% vs 15.4% for Doc vs LuP.
Conclusions: Doc has a greater detrimental impact on QOL than does LuP as determined by the FACT-P TOI, total FACT-P and most domain scores. Pts also reported more perceived side-effects with Doc, consistent with the global impact of treatment on QOL. Taken together, the PR21 trial findings suggest that LuP is better tolerated without demonstrable difference in rPFS compared to Doc.
Clinical trial identification: NCT04663997.
